decisive_items: history of excision of a dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans in the left inguinal–suprapubic region in 1998, with four local recurrences
two pulmonary nodules consistent with metastases

Fine-needle aspiration biopsy of the right lobe yielded a hemorrhagic background with isolated clusters of pleomorphic round and oval nuclei; it was classified as category IV/3, suspicious for primary or secondary malignancy
response.rationale: History of recurrent dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans with radiation exposure plus hemorrhagic pleomorphic FNA and pulmonary metastases favor metastatic disease to the thyroid over a primary thyroid carcinoma; anaplastic thyroid cancer is less supported by indolent 2-month course and mobile cords.

rejected.why: Papillary thyroid carcinoma typically has distinctive nuclear features and slower course; FNA is only suspicious, not diagnostic, and prior sarcoma history makes metastasis more likely.
Anaplastic thyroid cancer is aggressive and rapidly fatal; presentation with 2-month course and mobile cords is less supportive.
Same as R2 - anaplastic is less likely given subacute course and lack of fixation/invasion.
Medullary thyroid carcinoma would more likely show elevated calcitonin and different cytology; no supporting biochemical or imaging features.
